cities.name: Yerevan
interests: History & Ancient & Soviet Heritage 🏛️ — From pre-Christian temples and manuscripts to Soviet-era architecture.
Urban Culture & Street Life 🎨 — Cafés, wine streets, galleries and lively evening promenades.
Parks & Mountain Views 🌄 — Green spaces and viewpoints facing the iconic silhouette of Mount Ararat.
cities.local_food_tip: Lavash (flatbread), khorovats (barbecue), dolma, yogurt-based dishes and fresh vegetables — typical Armenian flavors with rustic charm. In Yerevan, look for places like Sherep Restaurant, Lavash Restaurant or Tavern Yerevan (Pandok) to try khorovats, tolma, spas (yogurt soup) and lavash straight from the tonir oven.
cities.full_day: Morning: 🕍 Start at Republic Square, the main central square with musical fountains, government buildings and the History Museum of Armenia and National Gallery on one side. → 🚶 Walk up Northern Avenue towards the Opera House and Swan Lake — lots of cafés and people-watching spots. → ⛰️ Climb (or use escalators inside) the Cascade Complex, stopping at the Cafesjian Center for the Arts for contemporary art and sculpture in and around the stairs. → ☕ Coffee break at one of the cafés at the base of the Cascade or in the surrounding Tamanyan Street garden. Afternoon: 🏛️ Head up Mashtots Avenue to the Matenadaran (Mesrop Mashtots Institute of Ancient Manuscripts), with thousands of illuminated manuscripts and a beautiful view over the city from its forecourt. → 🎭 Optionally visit smaller museums nearby, such as the Sergei Parajanov Museum overlooking the Hrazdan Gorge. → 🛍️ Walk through Vernissage Market, an open-air market with crafts, carpets, souvenirs and antiques near Republic Square. → 🍽️ Lunch at a traditional spot such as Tavern Yerevan (Pandok) or Sherep, with khorovats, dolma and salads. Late Afternoon: 🌳 Relax in Lovers’ Park or English Park, both green spaces in the central area. → Explore the old neighborhood of Kond, one of the oldest quarters with narrow lanes and more village-style houses right above the newer city. Sunset: 🌇 Climb back up the top platform of the Cascade or go to Victory Park for classic views over Yerevan with Mount Ararat in the background on a clear day. Night: 🌃 Head to Saryan Street (Wine Street) for wine bars and small restaurants, or explore café life and live music around Abovyan Street and Republic Square. → End with dessert or coffee at a place like Louis Charden or another central patisserie.

ideas: 🌸 Strolls through blooming Lovers’ Park, English Park and the green belts along the Circular Park.
🎨 Street art walks around Saryan Street and nearby creative quarters, plus galleries like the Cafesjian Center for the Arts at the Cascade.
☕ Outdoor cafés filling up along Northern Avenue and around the Opera House — perfect for people-watching.
📸 Clear spring air for photographing Republic Square, Cascade top viewpoint and Mount Ararat on the horizon.
🏞️ Day trips from Yerevan to nature spots like Garni Gorge, Lake Sevan or Dilijan National Park to escape the heat.
🌅 Evening walks around Cascade, Republic Square and Saryan Street with live music and fountain shows.
🍨 Ice cream and cold drinks in shaded spots near Swan Lake and along the central parks.
🌙 Open-air concerts and cultural nights around Republic Square and the Opera area.
🍂 Historic avenues like Abovyan Street and Mashtots Avenue under autumn foliage.
🥘 Warm traditional meals in cozy taverns such as Tavern Yerevan after cooler walks.
🏛️ Museum days at the Matenadaran, History Museum of Armenia and Cafesjian Center when weather is unpredictable.
📷 Golden-hour shots from Victory Park or the top of the Cascade as city lights start to glow.
❄️ Snow-dusted Republic Square with festive lights and decorated buildings.
🔥 Hot soups, khash and hearty Armenian dishes in traditional restaurants around the center.
🎄 Winter and holiday markets (when held) near main squares and along central streets.
☕ Long evenings in warm cafés near Northern Avenue and the Opera House, watching the city under soft lights.

public_transport_tips: 🚇 Yerevan has a simple metro system with one main line; central stations like Republic Square and Yeritasardakan are useful for visitors.
🚶 Many key sights — Republic Square, Cascade, Opera, Matenadaran — are within walking distance of each other.
🚍 City buses and minibuses cover most residential areas; for routes, locals often rely on apps like Moovit and online maps.
📱 For public transport directions, download Moovit on Android or Moovit on iOS, or use Google Maps transit directions around Yerevan.

city_events.name: Yerevan Summer Nights
city_events.description: 🎶 Open-air concerts, street performances and cultural nights around Republic Square, the Opera House and Cascade terraces under the stars.

city_events.name: Spring Art & Street Festival
city_events.description: 🎨 Murals, galleries, street art and creative workshops across central streets like Saryan Street and around the Cascade Complex.

city_events.name: Winter Holiday Market
city_events.description: 🎄 Festive decorations, local crafts, warm drinks and cozy atmosphere around Republic Square and nearby pedestrian streets.

cities.name: Dilijan
interests: Nature & Forests 🌲 — Lush woodland, mountain air and Dilijan National Park.
Hiking & Peaceful Retreats 🥾 — Trails, monasteries in the forest and quiet valleys.
Art & Traditional Crafts 🎨 — Old-town streets, wooden balconies and local artisans.
cities.local_food_tip: Rustic homemade bread, khashlama (slow-cooked meat), lentil and bean soups and village-style dairy — ideal after a forest walk or hike. Look for guesthouses or restaurants near the old quarter, such as those around the Old Dilijan (Tufenkian) Complex, where menus often feature homemade jams, herb salads and local honey.
cities.full_day: Morning: 🌄 Start your day at the Old Dilijan (Tufenkian) Complex, a restored street with traditional houses, balconies and craft shops — great for a gentle morning walk and photos. → ☕ Enjoy breakfast or coffee in a nearby café with mountain views. → 🌲 Then head toward Dilijan National Park area or a forest trailhead. Late Morning: 🥾 Take an easy hike around Parz Lake — a small lake in the forest with loop trails and rental boats in season. The path offers quiet, shady walking and plenty of photo spots. Afternoon: ⛪ After returning from Parz Lake, visit Haghartsin Monastery, a beautiful complex hidden in the forested hills, or Goshavank Monastery near the village of Gosh. → 🍽️ Have lunch at a village restaurant or guesthouse near one of these monasteries, sampling khashlama, grilled meats and fresh herbs. Late Afternoon: 🌳 Return to Dilijan and walk along the riverside in town or relax in one of the small parks. → 🎨 Explore local craft shops and galleries around the Old Dilijan quarter — woodcarving, handmade souvenirs and ceramics. Night: 🌙 Enjoy a quiet dinner in a family-run restaurant or guesthouse, then end the day with a short walk under the stars — Dilijan’s small-town atmosphere and forest surroundings give it a very calm, retreat-like feel.

ideas: 🌼 Blooming forest paths in Dilijan National Park with fresh scents and flowing streams.
🍃 Light picnic near Parz Lake or riverside meadows around Dilijan.
📸 Nature photography with misty mornings and new greenery around monasteries like Haghartsin.
☕ Relaxed coffee breaks in the Old Dilijan quarter after walks.
🏞️ Hiking to lakes and viewpoints in Dilijan National Park, escaping lower-country heat.
🌤️ Shady forest walks near Parz Lake or on trails between monasteries.
🌌 Starry nights from guesthouses on the hills around Dilijan, far from big-city lights.
🧺 Outdoor lunches and barbecues at picnic spots in the national park.
🍁 Golden and red leaves throughout Dilijan National Park — some of the most photogenic forests in Armenia.
🥘 Warm hearty meals in local taverns after long nature walks.
🖼️ Visits to craft workshops and small galleries in the Old Dilijan quarter on chilly days.
📷 Misty mornings in valleys and around Haghartsin Monastery — moody, atmospheric photos.
❄️ Snow-covered forests and quiet landscapes around Dilijan and nearby monasteries.
🔥 Hearth-side meals with local dishes and hot tea in guesthouses or small hotels.
🕯️ Peaceful night walks under crisp mountain air and clear skies when weather allows.
📚 Slow evenings with books and board games in cozy mountain accommodations.

public_transport_tips: 🚍 Regional minibuses (marshrutkas) from Yerevan’s Northern Bus Station commonly serve Dilijan — ask locally for current departure times.
🚶 The town center and nearby forest paths can often be reached on foot from many guesthouses.
🎒 Bring good walking shoes, rain jacket and layers — weather in the mountains can change quickly.
🚗 If driving, check road conditions in winter or rainy seasons, especially for side roads leading to Haghartsin, Goshavank and Parz Lake.

city_events.name: Forest & Nature Festival
city_events.description: 🌲 Guided hikes, eco-workshops and nature-focused activities in and around Dilijan National Park.

city_events.name: Autumn Crafts & Harvest Weekend
city_events.description: 🍂 Local food tastings, handicraft markets and village-style gatherings around the Old Dilijan quarter.

cities.name: Sevan Lake
interests: Lake & Water Activities 🌊 — High-altitude freshwater lake with beaches and boat rides.
Nature & Mountains 🏞️ — Hills, peninsulas and monastery viewpoints.
Relaxation & Scenic Views 🌅 — Quiet lakeside sunsets and cool summer breezes.
cities.local_food_tip: Fresh lake fish (especially Sevan trout and whitefish), grilled or baked, plus simple salads, lavash and local herbs — perfect after a swim or boat ride. Try lakeside restaurants around the Sevan Peninsula near Sevanavank Monastery for classic fish dishes with direct water views.
cities.full_day: Morning: 🌅 Arrive early at Sevan Peninsula and walk up to Sevanavank Monastery on the hill for beautiful morning light over the lake and surrounding mountains. → ⛪ Explore the small churches and stone crosses before the area gets busy. → ☕ Grab breakfast or coffee at a café near the peninsula, with terrace seating overlooking the water. Afternoon: 🏖️ Spend midday at one of the beaches along the western or northern shore — search for Sevan beach areas or private resorts around the lake. Swimming is popular in summer; off-season, enjoy long lakeside walks. → 🛶 In season, rent a boat or join a short cruise for wide-open views from the middle of the lake. → 🍽️ Lunch at a lakeside restaurant near the peninsula or in the town of Sevan town, with grilled fish, potatoes and salads. Late Afternoon: 🌳 Drive or walk to quieter parts of the shore, or head slightly inland to viewpoints overlooking the lake from higher ground. Some travelers combine Lake Sevan with a quick detour toward Dilijan National Park for a bit of forest scenery. Sunset: 🌇 Return to the Sevan Peninsula or another western-facing shore point to catch sunset colors over the water. The view from just below Sevanavank is especially dramatic. Night: 🌌 If staying overnight, enjoy a quiet evening at a lakeside hotel or guesthouse — listen to the waves, watch distant lights across the shore and enjoy a simple dinner with hot tea or wine.

ideas: 🌼 Mild weather and calm scenery along the shores near Sevan Peninsula — great for relaxed walks.
🐦 Birdwatching along quieter stretches of the lake and wetland areas.
📸 Photo sessions with bright blue water and snow still on distant peaks.
☕ Lakeside cafés near Sevanavank, open on sunny days for warm drinks with a view.
🏊 Swimming, sunbathing and water fun on Sevan beach areas — the classic Armenian summer escape.
🛶 Renting boats or taking short cruises from the peninsula area.
🌠 Evening bonfires or lakeside dinners with fish and fresh herbs at sunset.
🍦 Ice cream and cold drinks right by the lakeshore, especially near busier beach sections.
🍁 Quieter lakeshores and cooler but pleasant air — perfect for reflection and quiet walks.
🥘 Warm fish stews or grilled fish with hot tea in lakeside restaurants.
🌙 Evening strolls along the water under crisp skies with fewer crowds.
📷 Soft autumn light on Sevanavank and surrounding hills.
❄️ Snowy shores and near-empty beaches for a peaceful, minimal landscape.
🔥 Cozy meals in nearby lodges or guesthouses overlooking the lake.
🧭 Short winter hikes to viewpoints above the lake when conditions allow.
🕯️ Quiet nights watching snow and water from indoors with a warm drink.

public_transport_tips: 🚍 Regional buses and minibuses from Yerevan (often from the Kilikia Bus Station) go toward Sevan town and nearby villages.
🚶 Once at the lake or peninsula, many viewpoints and restaurants are reachable on foot; just be prepared for some uphill steps to Sevanavank.
🛶 In summer you can find local boat rentals near popular beach segments and the Sevan Peninsula.
🚗 Having a car makes it easier to explore quieter sections of the shoreline and combine Sevan with trips to Dilijan National Park.

city_events.name: Lake Sevan Summer Beach Days
city_events.description: ☀️ Beach time, boat rides, picnics and lakeside relaxation along the shores of Lake Sevan.

city_events.name: Autumn Lakeside Weekend
city_events.description: 🍂 Quiet weekends by the water with warm food, nature walks and calm atmosphere around the Sevan Peninsula.

cities.name: Gyumri
interests: Historic Architecture & Heritage 🏡 — Old stone houses, balconies and the Kumayri historic district.
Culture & Urban Life 🎭 — Art, humor, crafts and strong local character.
Mountain Views & Plateau Landscapes 🌄 — Open skies and distant peaks around the city.
cities.local_food_tip: Homemade dishes with meat, bread, potatoes and traditional recipes — very comforting and rich. Around the center, look for places such as Polos Restaurant or small family taverns near Vardanants Square for khorovats, soups and fresh bread.
cities.full_day: Morning: 🏘️ Begin at Vardanants Square, the main square of Gyumri, surrounded by churches, cafés and historic buildings. → ⛪ Visit Yot Verk (Seven Wounds) Church and the nearby Holy Mother of God Cathedral. → ☕ Enjoy breakfast or coffee in one of the cafés facing the square. Late Morning: 🏛️ Wander through the Kumayri Historic District, with its old black tuff stone houses, carved balconies and cobblestone streets — many buildings show both pre-Soviet and Soviet-era styles. → 🖼️ Visit a small museum such as the Dzitoghtsyan Museum of Social Life and National Architecture to see traditional interiors and local history. Afternoon: 🌳 Head to Gyumri Central Park or other green areas for a relaxed walk. → 🍽️ Have lunch at a local restaurant — try khashlama, tolma or homemade-style soups along with bread from local bakeries. Late Afternoon: 🏰 If you have transport, visit the Black Fortress (Sev Berd) outside town, an old 19th-century Russian-era fort with views over Gyumri and the plateau. → 📸 Take photos of the city from viewpoints around Sev Berd or nearby hills. Night: 🌃 Return to the center for a calm evening — a walk around Vardanants Square and adjacent streets lit up. → Enjoy dinner in a cozy tavern and maybe coffee and sweets at a local spot before calling it a night.

ideas: 🌿 Blossoming trees and mild temperatures for exploring the Kumayri historic district on foot.
🎭 Cultural events, performances and local gatherings often centered around Vardanants Square.
📷 Photography of historic façades and streets before the summer crowds.
☕ Street cafés opening their terraces around the main squares.
🏞️ Day trips into nearby countryside and villages around Gyumri for open plateau landscapes.
🌇 Evening walks through the center, from Vardanants Square into residential streets with old architecture.
🍧 Ice cream, cold drinks and light meals in local cafés on warm evenings.
🎶 Occasional concerts or street performances, especially in central squares and parks.
🍁 Historic streets under warm autumn light — ideal for relaxed photography and slow walks.
🥘 Traditional meals and cultural evenings in taverns with a strong local character.
🎶 Folk music nights or gatherings in community spaces and restaurants.
📚 Museum visits in cooler weather, such as the Dzitoghtsyan Museum.
❄️ Snowy streets and roofs in the Kumayri district, giving the city a very atmospheric look.
🔥 Warm local meals — stews, soups and hot drinks in family-run cafés after walks.
🕯️ Quiet nights under soft street lighting, showing Gyumri’s slower rhythm.
📸 Winter photography of the Black Fortress and surrounding plains.

public_transport_tips: 🚍 Regional buses and trains connect Gyumri with Yerevan and other cities; check schedules at the Gyumri railway station or main bus terminals.
🚶 The central part of Gyumri — including Vardanants Square and the Kumayri historic district — is very walkable.
🚗 For visiting rural areas or the Black Fortress, taxis or a rented car can be convenient, especially in winter.
📅 Spring and autumn offer the most comfortable climate for walking tours, while winter can be quite cold and snowy.

city_events.name: Gyumri Cultural Weekend
city_events.description: 🎭 Concerts, cultural festivals and local gatherings celebrating Gyumri’s artistic heritage around Vardanants Square and nearby venues.

city_events.name: Winter Heritage & Food Fair
city_events.description: 🍲 Local food tastings, traditional dishes and community events set in historic halls and cafés across the Kumayri district.

cities.name: Tatev Monastery & Surroundings
interests: Medieval Monastery & Spiritual Heritage ⛪ — Tatev Monastery complex on a dramatic plateau.
Mountain Scenery & Cliff Views 🏔️ — Deep canyons, high ridges and vast horizons.
Hiking & Rural Village Life 🚶 — Trails, villages and slow-paced countryside life.
cities.local_food_tip: Rustic dishes with local vegetables, home-baked bread, roasted lamb, herbs and regional cheeses — perfect after mountain walks. 🍖🍞 Look for guesthouses and home-style restaurants around the villages near Tatev village or at the lower Halidzor station area.
cities.full_day: Morning: 🏞️ Start at the Halidzor station of the Wings of Tatev aerial tramway, which crosses the Vorotan Gorge to reach the monastery. → 🚡 Enjoy the 10–12 minute ride over the canyon with stunning views. → ⛪ Arrive at Tatev Monastery and explore the courtyards, churches and cliff-edge viewpoints. Afternoon: 🥾 Take a short hike from the monastery or village toward nearby viewpoints and trails, such as paths leading to observation spots above the gorge. → 🍽️ Have lunch in a village guesthouse or small restaurant in Tatev village, with simple hearty meals, fresh herbs and homemade preserves. → 🌿 Spend some time walking through the village itself, seeing traditional stone houses and rural life. Late Afternoon: 🌄 Ride the Wings of Tatev tramway back to Halidzor, enjoying the shifting light in the canyon. If you have a car, you can stop at roadside viewpoints along the serpentine road or combine the trip with nearby sites like Devil’s Bridge. Sunset: 🌅 Watch sunset from a viewpoint near Tatev or from a terrace at a guesthouse overlooking the valley — the changing colors on cliffs and hills are dramatic. Night: 🌌 Stay overnight in a local guesthouse, enjoying dinner by a fireplace, local wine and a very quiet mountain night with brilliant stars.

ideas: 🌼 Green hillsides, wildflowers and flowing waterfalls in the Vorotan Gorge near Tatev Monastery.
🕯️ Quieter monastery atmosphere before peak tourist season, ideal for reflective visits.
📸 Dramatic landscapes for photography from the Wings of Tatev aerial tram and nearby overlooks.
🥾 Comfortable temperatures for moderate hikes around Tatev village and the canyon edges.
🏔️ Cool mountain air and wide panoramas from Tatev Monastery plateau.
🍃 Fresh outdoor meals, picnics and rest stops in village gardens and terraces.
🌠 Exceptionally starry nights in rural guesthouses, far from big city light.
🚡 Frequent runs of the Wings of Tatev tramway make it easy to combine hiking and monastery visits.
🍂 Golden and red foliage on the slopes around Tatev and along the Vorotan Gorge.
🔥 Hearty local meals and warm hospitality in guesthouses as evenings turn chilly.
🛖 Slow village life — time to chat with locals, learn about traditions and enjoy a slower pace.
📷 Crystal-clear air and softer light for photos of monasteries, canyons and villages.
❄️ Snow-dusted monastery walls and quiet paths around Tatev — very atmospheric if the road and tram are operating.
🔥 Fireside dinners and hot soups after brief cold walks outside.
🕯️ Early nights, candlelight and thick blankets in rural guesthouses — calm and introspective.
🚶 Short winter walks around the village when conditions are safe, observing mountain silence.

public_transport_tips: 🚍 Minibuses from Yerevan or Goris can get you to towns near Tatev; from there you may need a taxi or transfer to reach the Halidzor station or Tatev village.
🚡 The Wings of Tatev aerial tram is the most scenic way to reach the monastery and is a highlight in itself.
🚶 Once at Tatev, exploring the monastery and village is done entirely on foot, so comfortable shoes are important.
🚗 A private car or arranged tour provides the most flexibility, especially if you want to include stops like Devil’s Bridge or other viewpoints — always check road conditions in winter.

city_events.name: Tatev Heritage & Nature Day
city_events.description: 🙏 Traditional ceremonies, heritage tours, music and guided hikes around Tatev Monastery and the surrounding villages.

city_events.name: Autumn Mountain & Culture Weekend
city_events.description: 🌄 Guided walks, local food tastings and cultural exchanges in the villages around Tatev and along the Vorotan Gorge.

cities.name: Garni & Geghard (Temple & Monastery Region)
interests: Ancient History & Pagan Temple Ruins 🏛️ — Garni Temple, a classical colonnaded structure from pre-Christian Armenia.
Medieval Monastery & Rock-Carved Church ⛪ — Geghard, carved into rock and cliffs.
Nature, Rivers & Canyon Landscapes 🌄 — Azat River gorge, basalt columns and dramatic valleys.
cities.local_food_tip: Fresh vegetables, homemade bread, local cheese, barbecued meats and lavash baked in traditional tonirs — wholesome meals after exploring history and nature. In the village of Garni you’ll often find homes and small eateries offering traditional bread-making demos and lunches near the Garni Temple area.
cities.full_day: Morning: 🏛️ Drive from Yerevan to Garni Temple, a reconstructed Greco-Roman style pagan temple on a cliff above the Azat River gorge. → 🚶 Walk around the temple platform for views over the canyon and surrounding mountains. → ⛰️ If you have time, hike or take a vehicle down into Garni Gorge to see the “Symphony of Stones” basalt columns and river scenery. Afternoon: ⛪ Continue to Geghard Monastery, a UNESCO-listed site partly carved into the rock cliffs. Explore the courtyards, chapels and rock-hewn halls with atmospheric acoustics. → 🕯️ Listen to the echo of singing if a choir or pilgrims are present — it’s very special in the carved chambers. → 🍽️ Have lunch in a nearby village restaurant or guesthouse on the road between Garni and Geghard, with kebabs, fresh herbs, lavash and homemade jams. Late Afternoon: 🥾 Optionally take short walks on paths above or around the monastery to see different angles of the cliffs and valley. → 🛍️ Stop by roadside stalls selling sweet sujukh (walnut sweets), dried fruits and local honey. Sunset: 🌅 Drive back towards Garni or Yerevan, stopping at a viewpoint overlooking the Azat River canyon or the surrounding mountains. On a clear day the light over the rocks and temple area is beautiful. Night: 🌌 Return to Yerevan or stay in a nearby guesthouse in Garni or a surrounding village for a quieter countryside night with local food and starry skies.

ideas: 🌼 Pleasant temperatures for walking around Garni Temple and along the canyon edge.
📚 Quieter visits to Geghard Monastery before peak tourist season.
🌿 Green valleys and flowing river in Garni Gorge — great for photography and short hikes.
☕ Relaxing lunches and tea on village terraces with views of fields and cliffs.
🏞️ Combine culture and nature: visit Garni Temple, then cool down in the breezy Azat River gorge.
🥾 Light hikes around cliffs and rivers near Garni and paths leading to viewpoints above Geghard.
🍨 Ice cream or cold drinks in the village of Garni after a hot temple visit.
🎶 Occasional cultural or musical events near Garni Temple during festivals.
🍂 Golden hillsides and softer light around Garni and Geghard — perfect for photos.
🔥 Warm village meals and fresh-baked lavash after exploring historical sites.
🎶 Evening calm and occasional traditional music in guesthouses or small taverns.
📷 Sunset shots over canyon cliffs and temple columns in cooler, clear weather.
❄️ Snow on the columns of Garni Temple and on cliffs around Geghard — very atmospheric if roads are passable.
🔥 Warm soups and stews in local eateries after brisk walks around the sites.
🕯️ Quiet monastery atmosphere at Geghard, with chanting echoing in rock-hewn chambers.
🚶 Short winter walks along the roads and village paths with views of bare cliffs and valleys.

public_transport_tips: 🚍 Minibuses from Yerevan (often leaving near central bus points) go to the village of Garni; from there, a taxi or hike can get you to Garni Temple.
🚶 Exploring sites like Garni Temple, Garni Gorge and Geghard Monastery is mostly done on foot along roads and trails.
🚗 A car or organized tour makes it easier to combine Garni and Geghard in one day and stop at scenic overlooks on the way.
📅 Spring and early autumn are usually the most comfortable months to visit, avoiding intense summer heat and potential winter road issues.

city_events.name: Ancient Heritage Day
city_events.description: 🏛️ Guided tours, storytelling and cultural activities focused on the history of Garni Temple and Geghard Monastery.

city_events.name: Autumn Culture & Nature Weekend
city_events.description: 🍂 A combination of canyon hikes, temple and monastery visits and local cuisine in villages around Garni and Geghard.
